page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.large is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a sustained clock speed of 5.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance includes 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without local instance storage, relying entirely on remote Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded performance driven by the 5.0 GHz processor frequency and AVX-512 vector instruction capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression at 46.3 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 20.59 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core evaluations with a score of 3126.0. Geekbench text processing also lands in the top decile. In contrast, multi-core throughput across stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark tests sits in the median range due to the two-core allocation. Lower relative scores are observed in compute-heavy ray tracing, PassMark memory scoring, and medium-sized LLM prompt processing.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the m8azn.large delivers high compute efficiency for workloads constrained by clock speed rather than parallel execution width. The high memory frequency and dedicated core configuration prevent noisy-neighbor contention common in shared-thread platforms. However, the absence of local NVMe storage necessitates factoring in EBS input/output dependencies for storage-heavy architectures. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, API backends, Redis key-value caching, text-parsing pipelines, and single-thread intensive batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.large is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor with 2 dedicated cores clocked at 5.0 GHz. Equipped with 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance delivers 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and relies on network-attached storage, with no integrated local disks or GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile performance in single-core compute, compression, and text manipulation tasks, whereas multi-core throughput and memory subsystem benchmarks reflect expected constraints from its two-core profile. With dedicated physical cores and high frequency, m8azn.large is well aligned with workloads demanding robust single-threaded compute density, including web applications, Redis caching, microservices, and targeted data processing utilities.
